According to the wording of the question, the sample size n = 100, the number of blue balloons x = 30, so the sample proportion is p̂ = 30/100 = 0.30. When constructing a 95% confidence interval for the population proportion, using the normal approximation method, take z* = 1.96, and the standard error is SE = √(p̂(1-p̂)/n) = √(0.30×0.70/100) ≈ 0.0458, and the margin of error is 1.96×0.0458 ≈ 0.0898. method.method_draft: Use the numerical data in the question to compute a one-sample large-sample confidence interval for a population proportion. From the text, identify n = 100 and x = 30, so the sample proportion is p-hat = 30/100 = 0.30. For a 95% confidence interval, use z* = 1.96. Compute the standard error sqrt(p-hat(1 - p-hat)/n) = sqrt(0.30 * 0.70 / 100), then form p-hat ± 1.96 times this standard error. Round the resulting endpoints to three decimals and report the interval, noting that the supplied standard/image answer gives (0.210, 0.399).
